quote: Domain Generalized Semantic Segmentation (DGSS) aims for strong performance across unseen domains without relying on target domain data during training.
claim: DGSS problem formulation: training on source domain only to generalize to unseen target domains without target data access

quote: We propose a novel fusion framework, MFuser, to collaborate arbitrary pairs of VFMs and VLMs for DGSS, integrating the strengths of both without introducing significant computational overhead.
claim: Main contribution: MFuser framework fuses Vision Foundation Models and Vision Language Models for domain generalization

quote: Specifically, we introduce MVFuser, a Mamba-based co-adapter that jointly fine-tunes the two Visual models.
claim: Key method: MVFuser uses Mamba-based state-space model for parameter-efficient joint fine-tuning of VFM and VLM encoders

quote: Extensive experiments show the proposed MFuser consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods, achieving 68.20 mIoU on synthetic-to-real and 71.87 mIoU on real-to-real benchmarks.
claim: Main experimental finding: MFuser achieves SOTA performance with 68.20 mIoU on synthetic-to-real and 71.87 mIoU on real-to-real DGSS benchmarks

quote: Based on these observations, we introduced a novel framework named SCSD, which is designed to explore Semantic Consistency and Style Diversity for DGSS.
claim: Main contribution: SCSD framework leverages Vision-Language Models for semantic consistency and style diversity in DGSS

quote: Secondly, we introduce a Text-Driven Style Transformation (TDST) module that mines the style diversity of the text modality.
claim: Key method: TDST uses text prompt differences to guide controllable style transformation of image features via Fourier transform

quote: Notably, SCSD outperforms the state-of-the-art methods by up to +4.87 and +2.92 mIoU on unseen Mapillary and ACDC domains, respectively.
claim: Main experimental finding: SCSD achieves SOTA improvements of +4.87 mIoU on Mapillary and +2.92 mIoU on ACDC benchmarks

quote: Unlike DASS, which requires access to target domain data during training, an often impractical requirement, Domain Generalized Semantic Segmentation (DGSS) offers a promising alternative.
claim: DGSS problem formulation: learning from source domain only without requiring target domain data during training

quote: how to learn style-invariant representation by fine-tuning VFMs? Spectral decomposition has been long acknowledged effective to handle the style and content information separately in the context of domain generalization
claim: SET addresses the key challenge of learning style-invariant representations by leveraging spectral decomposition to separate style and content information

quote: we design a token-based feature enhancement pipeline which extracts task-specific information and adjusts the spectral-decomposed features in amplitude and phase branches separately
claim: The method uses learnable tokens to enhance spectral-decomposed features in separate amplitude and phase branches

quote: our proposed BlindNet consists of two components: covariance alignment for the encoder and semantic consistency contrastive learning for the decoder
claim: BlindNet addresses domain shift through encoder covariance alignment and decoder contrastive learning without requiring auxiliary datasets

quote: We propose a covariance alignment within the encoder, comprising CML and CCL. Specifically, the CML aims to mitigate the effects of style variations, while CCL ensures the preservation of content information
claim: The covariance matching loss (CML) mitigates style variations while cross-covariance loss (CCL) preserves content information

quote: the proposed CCL converges only the diagonal component of the covariance matrix to one. This is to prevent the drawbacks of the existing FN methods from removing content information
claim: CCL selectively preserves content information by converging only diagonal covariance components, avoiding the content loss problem of feature normalization methods

quote: existing methods in DGSS have not yet explored direct language-driven approaches to utilize textual representations from VLMs for domain-generalized recognition
claim: tqdm is the first language-driven DGSS method that directly utilizes textual representations from Vision-Language Models

quote: The key idea of our method is to utilize text embeddings of classes of interest from VLMs as object queries, referred to as textual object queries
claim: The method uses text embeddings from VLMs as textual object queries to enable domain-invariant semantic recognition

quote: we maintain E_T frozen to preserve its original language representations. For the second requirement, we employ learnable prompts to adapt textual features from E_T
claim: The text encoder is kept frozen to preserve domain-invariant language representations while learnable prompts adapt features for segmentation

quote: we approach DG differently from other methods by focusing on synthesizing data instead of model architectures or training techniques
claim: DGInStyle takes a novel data synthesis approach to domain generalization rather than modifying model architectures or training techniques

quote: we propose a novel Style Swap technique inspired by modern fine-tuning and semantic style control mechanisms, to achieve the necessary level of control and diversity over the outputs
claim: Style Swap technique decouples semantic control from style, allowing learning of dense semantic control while removing source domain style bias

section: 3.2 Preserving Style Prior with Style Swap
quote: This enables us to apply semantic control learned from the source domain to the original LDM. The overall procedure endows the original LDM with task-specific semantic control
claim: Style Swap enables applying source-domain-learned semantic control to the original LDM, preserving rich style prior knowledge

quote: In this work, we introduce a robust and efficient fine-tuning approach, namely "Rein". Tailored for DGSS tasks, Rein employs fewer trainable parameters to harness stronger VFMs for achieving superior generalization.
claim: Rein introduces a parameter-efficient fine-tuning method for Vision Foundation Models in domain generalized semantic segmentation

quote: At its core, Rein comprises a set of randomly initialized tokens, each directly linked to different instances. These tokens, through a dot-product operation with VFMs features, generate an attention-like similarity map.
claim: Rein uses learnable tokens linked to instances for instance-level feature refinement through attention-like mechanisms

quote: This paper shows that we can prevent such behavior with a simple recipe involving minimal fine-tuning, language-driven style augmentation, and mixing. Our approach is coined FAMix, for Freeze, Augment and Mix.
claim: FAMix proposes a three-component framework for DGSS using CLIP: minimal fine-tuning, language-driven augmentation, and style mixing

quote: We propose language-driven class-wise local style augmentation. We mine class-specific local statistics using prompts that express random styles and names of patch-wise dominant classes.
claim: FAMix introduces language-driven style mining using prompts combining random styles with class names for domain augmentation

quote: Previous works suggest that shallow feature statistics capture style information while deeper features encode semantic content. Consequently, some DGSS methods focus on learning style-agnostic representations, but this can compromise the expressiveness of the representation and suppress content information.
claim: FAMix preserves shallow feature style information while training final layers for invariant high-level representations

quote: In this work, we propose a novel method that tackles the domain generalization problem by diffusion-based domain extension (DIDEX). Diffusion models have demonstrated remarkable capabilities in capturing complex distributions and semantics and generating realistic samples with high quality.
claim: DIDEX leverages diffusion models to generate realistic pseudo-target domains for domain generalization without real target data

quote: The crucial advantage of diffusion models is the prompt-based control of the generated image. That enables us to define the content and style of the generated images and create a pseudo-target domain D^{PT}.
claim: DIDEX uses text prompts to control diffusion model generation of diverse pseudo-target domains covering location, weather, and content variations

quote: Our method changes this setting slightly but notably to UDA(D^{S},D^{PT})\rightarrow M^{DG} , where model M is adapted to our pseudo-target domain D^{PT} and therefore also generalizes without accessing any real data.
claim: DIDEX adapts UDA techniques to train on synthetic pseudo-target domains instead of real target domains, enabling generalization without real data access

quote: Driven by the motivation of narrowing down the research gap, in this work we propose to amalgamate an assembly of FMs into a cohesive system to address DGSS. In detail, we propose to exploit: (i) strong representations of contrastive FMs, (ii) diverse content augmentation using generative FMs, and (iii) near accurate class-agnostic mask prediction of SAM and turn them into semantic predictions.
claim: CLOUDS combines multiple foundation models: CLIP for features, diffusion models for content augmentation, and SAM for pseudo-label refinement

quote: We highlight for the first time in DGSS the importance of content diversification, which is more effective than traditional DGSS methods relying on style diversification
claim: CLOUDS demonstrates that content diversification through generative models outperforms traditional style diversification approaches in DGSS

quote: The pseudo labels generated by the teacher decoder demonstrate prediction inaccuracies. For their refinement, we use SAM, capable of generating multiple detailed masks for any image within a zero-shot framework.
claim: CLOUDS uses SAM with point-based prompting to refine noisy pseudo-labels from the teacher decoder in self-training

quote: in our pipeline, learnable tokens are utilized to refine the spectral components \alpha_{k} and \rho_{k} of features at each layer within the frozen VFM backbone
claim: Spectral tokens refine features in the frequency domain while keeping the VFM backbone frozen for efficient fine-tuning
